paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: the Christian life is a race, and you don't run it alone or on your own strength. The writer says we're "surrounded by such a great cloud of witnesses," so throw off every encumbrance and the sin that so easily entangles, and "run with endurance the race set out for us" (Hebrews 12:1). Then he tells us where to look. "Let us fix our eyes on Jesus, the author and perfecter of our faith," who "for the joy set before Him endured the cross" (Hebrews 12:2).

Now the hard part, and the writer doesn't dodge it. Discipline is not fun. "No discipline seems enjoyable at the time, but painful" (Hebrews 12:11). I've had my share of squished, stamped and shoved into a drawer, and I did NOT enjoy it either! But the writer says "the Lord disciplines the one He loves" (Hebrews 12:6), so a hard season is no sign that God has walked away. He disciplines us "for our good, so that we may share in His holiness," and later on it "yields a harvest of righteousness and peace" (Hebrews 12:10-11).

So what do you do when you're tired? You "strengthen your limp hands and weak knees" (Hebrews 12:12). You keep your eyes on Jesus, you don't lose heart, and you trust the Father who is shaping you. And you run so that others can follow, because the writer says to make straight paths for your feet, "so that the lame may not be disabled, but rather healed" (Hebrews 12:13). Keep running, baker. The finish line is worth it!
